cards.q: Find the next term: 6, 11, 16, 21, 26, ___.
cards.why: Each term is 5 more than the one before: 26 + 5 = 31. The next term would be 36, so the gap stays 5.
cards.trap: Adding 6 to 26 to answer 32, or doubling the gap to answer 36.

cards.q: Find the next term: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48, ___.
cards.why: Each term doubles: 48 x 2 = 96. Doubling again gives 192, so the rule holds.
cards.trap: Using gaps 3, 6, 12, 24, 36 and answering 84.

cards.why: Two sequences interleave. Odd places go 2, 5, 8, 11, so add 3: 14. Even places go 10, 20, 30, 40.
cards.trap: Adding 10 to 40 and answering 50, or adding 2 to 11 and answering 13.

cards.q: Find the next term: 3, 4, 8, 15, 25, ___.
cards.why: Gaps are 1, 4, 7, 10, which rise by 3 each time. The next gap is 13, so 25 + 13 = 38.
cards.trap: Repeating the gap 10 and answering 35.

cards.q: Find the next term: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ___.
cards.why: These are squares: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36. The gaps 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 also give 25 + 11 = 36.
cards.trap: Keeping the gap at 9 and answering 34.

cards.q: Find the next term: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, ___.
cards.why: These are cubes: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216. The next cube is 343, so 6^3 = 216 fits.
cards.trap: Doubling 125 to answer 250, or jumping to 7^3 = 343.

cards.q: Find the next term: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ___.
cards.why: Each term is double the one before, plus 1: 2 x 63 + 1 = 127. The next term is 2 x 127 + 1 = 255.
cards.trap: Doubling 63 to answer 128, or repeating gap 32 to answer 95.

cards.q: Find the next term: 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ___.
cards.why: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 13 + 21 = 34. The next term is 21 + 34 = 55.
cards.trap: Repeating the last gap 8 and answering 29.

cards.q: Find the next term: 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, ___.
cards.why: These are the primes in order: 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. The next prime is 23.
cards.trap: Treating 21 as prime and answering 21.

cards.q: Find the next term: 2, 6, 24, 120, 720, ___.
cards.why: Multiply by 3, then 4, then 5, then 6: 720 x 7 = 5040. The next term is 5040 x 8 = 40320.
cards.trap: Multiplying 720 by 6 again and answering 4320.

cards.why: Add the digit sum of each term: 14 + 5 = 19, 19 + 10 = 29, and so on. 59 + 14 = 73. The next term is 83.
cards.trap: Adding the last gap 7 again and answering 66.

cards.q: Find the next term: 51, 50, 47, 41, 31, ___.
cards.why: Subtract 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 in turn. The steps are triangular, so 31 - 15 = 16. The next term is 16 - 21 = -5.
cards.trap: Repeating the last step of 10 and answering 21.

cards.q: Find the next letter: C, F, I, L, O, ___.
cards.why: Each letter moves 3 places forward: C, F, I, L, O, R. The next letter is U.
cards.trap: Counting C as 1 and shifting the series, answering Q.

cards.q: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ___.
cards.why: The skips grow by one: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. O plus 6 places is U. The next skip of 7 gives B.
cards.trap: Keeping the skip at 5 and answering T.

cards.q: Find the next letter: A, Z, C, X, E, V, ___.
cards.why: Odd places move forward 2: A, C, E, G. Even places move back 2: Z, X, V. The blank is odd, so G.
cards.trap: Adding 3 to E to answer H, as if the forward skips grew.

cards.q: What comes next? O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ___.
cards.why: These are the first letters of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven. Eight starts with E. Nine starts with N.
cards.trap: Repeating S because the last two letters are S.

cards.q: Find the next letter: Z, X, V, T, R, ___.
cards.why: Each letter moves 2 places back in the alphabet: Z, X, V, T, R, P. The next letter is N.
cards.trap: Moving back one place and answering Q.

cards.q: Find the next letter: A, B, E, D, I, F, O, H, ___.
cards.why: Odd places are the vowels A, E, I, O, U. Even places are consonants B, D, F, H. The blank is odd, so U.
cards.trap: Continuing the consonants H, J and answering J.

cards.q: If CAT is coded as FDW, how is DOG coded?
cards.why: Each letter shifts 3 places forward: C to F, A to D, T to W. So D, O, G become G, R, J.
cards.trap: Shifting only the first letter and answering FRJ, or slipping a place to answer GRK.

cards.q: If NOTE is coded as GVQP, how is LAMP coded?
cards.why: Reverse the word, then shift each letter 2 forward. LAMP reversed is PMAL, which becomes R, O, C, N.
cards.trap: Shifting without reversing, giving NCOR.

cards.q: Letters map to positions, so A=1, B=2, up to Z=26. If CAB is 3,1,2, what is FAD?
cards.why: F is 6, A is 1, and D is 4, so FAD is 6,1,4 in order. The position of A is 1, not 0.
cards.trap: Using A=0 and answering 5,1,4.

cards.q: Each letter shifts forward by its place in the word: first by 1, second by 2, third by 3. If CAT becomes DCW, what is DOG?
cards.why: D plus 1 is E, O plus 2 is Q, G plus 3 is J. So DOG becomes EQJ.
cards.trap: Adding 4 to G and answering EQK, as if the shift kept growing.

cards.q: Letters shift +3, then -2, then +3, then -2, and so on. If CAT becomes FYW, what is BOLD?
cards.why: B plus 3 is E, O minus 2 is M, L plus 3 is O, D minus 2 is B. So BOLD becomes EMOB.
cards.trap: Subtracting 3 instead of 2 from O and answering ELOB.

cards.q: In a code each letter moves 3 places back. If TRIM becomes QOFJ, what is STOP?
cards.why: S minus 3 is P, T minus 3 is Q, O minus 3 is L, P minus 3 is M. So STOP becomes PQLM.
cards.trap: Subtracting 2 from the last letter and answering PQLN.

cards.q: Four of these are perfect squares: 9, 25, 36, 42, 49. Which is not?
cards.why: 9, 25, 36, and 49 are the squares of 3, 5, 6, and 7. 42 is not a square, since 6^2 = 36 and 7^2 = 49.
cards.trap: Calling 42 a square because it sits between 36 and 49.

cards.q: Four of these are prime numbers: 11, 13, 15, 17, 19. Which is not?
cards.why: 11, 13, 17, and 19 have no divisors except 1 and themselves. 15 equals 3 x 5, so it is composite.
cards.trap: Treating 15 as prime because it is odd.

cards.q: Four of these are multiples of 7: 21, 28, 35, 42, 48. Which is not?
cards.why: 21, 28, 35, and 42 are 3x7, 4x7, 5x7, and 6x7. 48 leaves a remainder of 6 when divided by 7.
cards.trap: Assuming 48 is a multiple because 42 and 49 are close.

cards.q: Four of these are perfect cubes: 27, 64, 81, 125, 216. Which is not?
cards.trap: Calling 81 a cube because it is a power of 3.

cards.q: Four of these divide 120 exactly: 8, 12, 15, 16, 24. Which does not?
cards.why: 120 divided by 8, 12, 15, and 24 gives whole numbers. 120 divided by 16 is 7.5, so 16 does not divide 120 exactly.
cards.trap: Assuming every even number below 24 divides 120.

cards.q: Four of these are triangular numbers: 10, 15, 21, 28, 35. Which is not?
cards.why: Triangular numbers add 1, 2, 3, and so on: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, 36. So 35 is not triangular.
cards.trap: Extending gaps 5, 6, 7 with another 7 and accepting 35 as triangular.
